title: Trees and Binary Trees: The Words GATE Uses
quickIdea: A tree of n nodes has exactly n-1 edges and one path between any two nodes; a binary tree adds a left and a right position and caps a node at two children, and the leaf count follows from the degree count.
remember: A tree on n nodes has exactly n-1 edges. Add an edge and a cycle appears; remove an edge and the structure splits into two trees.

Root, parent, child, sibling, leaf (no children), internal node (at least one child). The level of the root is 0, the depth of a node is its number of edges from the root, and the height of the tree is the largest depth in it.

In a binary tree each node has at most two children, and the left and right slots are different even when only one is filled. That is why the same preorder and postorder can come from two different binary trees.

Full (also called strict or proper) means every node has 0 or 2 children. Complete means every level except possibly the last is full and the last level is filled from the left. Perfect means full and all leaves at the same depth. Complete is not full, and perfect is both.

For any non-empty binary tree, leaves = nodes with two children + 1. The identity comes from counting edges two ways and needs no full-tree assumption: n = n0 + n1 + n2 and n - 1 = n1 + 2n2 give n0 = n2 + 1.
GATE states its own convention when it matters. Questions that say the height of a single node is 0 are counting edges, not levels.

example.prompt: A binary tree has root 1, children 2 and 3, and 2 has children 4 and 5. Count nodes, edges, leaves and two-child nodes, and give the height and the depth of node 5.
example.work: Nodes: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, so n = 5 and the edges are 1-2, 1-3, 2-4, 2-5, which is 4 = n - 1. Leaves: 3, 4, 5, so n0 = 3. Two-child nodes: 1 and 2, so n2 = 2, and n0 = n2 + 1 holds. The longest root-to-leaf path is 1-2-4, two edges, so the height is 2. Node 5 is reached by 1-2-5, also two edges, so its depth is 2.
example.answer: n = 5, edges = 4, leaves = 3, two-child nodes = 2, height = 2, depth of node 5 = 2.

gateAngle: Terminology questions are usually a count: the leaf identity in GATE CSE 2025 Set 2 Q.3, the height convention in the note attached to GATE CSE 2017 Set 1 Q.6, and the full versus complete distinction that decides whether a node with one child is allowed.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: GATE CSE 2025 Set 2 Q.3. A binary tree T has n > 0 nodes and every node has either zero or two children. How many nodes have exactly two children?
variations.why: Every node is a leaf or a two-child node, so n = n0 + n2, and the edge count gives n - 1 = 2n2. Dividing, n2 = (n - 1)/2. Equivalently n0 = n2 + 1, so n = 2n2 + 1.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: A binary tree has 5 nodes with two children and some leaves, and every other node is a leaf. How many leaves does it have, and how many nodes in total?
variations.why: n0 = n2 + 1 = 6, so n = n0 + n2 = 6 + 5 = 11. The identity holds because no node has exactly one child here, which is the case the formula is usually memorised for, but the edge-counting proof does not need it.

trap.what: Believing that leaves = internal nodes + 1 needs a full binary tree, or that a complete binary tree cannot contain a node with one child.
trap.why: The identity leaves = two-child nodes + 1 comes from counting edges, and it survives nodes with one child; what breaks it is replacing it by leaves = internal nodes + 1 when internal nodes include one-child nodes.
trap.counterexample: A complete binary tree on 4 nodes: root with left child and right child, and the left child has a left child. The node with one child exists, so the tree is not full, yet leaves = 2 and two-child nodes = 1, so leaves = two-child nodes + 1. Internal nodes number 2, and leaves = internal nodes + 1 would be false.

check.question: A binary tree has 9 nodes and every internal node has exactly two children. How many leaves and how many internal nodes does it have?
check.explanation: n = n0 + n2 and n0 = n2 + 1 give 9 = 2n2 + 1, so n2 = 4 and n0 = 5. The edge count agrees: 8 edges, and 4 two-child nodes produce 8 edges.
